channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Após decisão sobre prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro, Flávio chama Moraes de 'sem alma' em evento do PL no ES
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro harshly criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, calling him 'soulless' and comparing him to a 'demon using a person to do harm,' during a PL event in Espírito Santo. The remarks followed Moraes’ decision to maintain Jair Bolsonaro’s house arrest and restrict visits with political-electoral purposes until the end of the 2026 elections. Flávio also advocated for strengthening the right-wing bloc in Congress and expressed hope of reuniting with his father soon.

item.title: Zema promete privatizar Petrobras e Banco do Brasil e usar recursos em obras de infraestrutura
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo Party's pre-candidate for the 2026 Brazilian presidency, pledged to privatize Petrobras and Banco do Brasil to fund nationwide infrastructure projects such as highways, railways, and ports. He criticized President Lula, affirmative action policies, and progressive education, while advocating to label criminal factions as terrorist organizations with minimum 25-year sentences. Zema also stated he aims to build a Senate majority to impeach Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Brasil colhe o que Lula plantou com tarifa dos EUA, diz Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, pré-presidential candidate from Novo, blamed the Lula government for the new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, claiming foreign policy provoked tensions with Washington through rapprochement with Venezuela, Cuba, and Iran. He stated Brazil 'reaped what it sowed,' arguing the burden falls on productive sectors and taxpayers, not the political elite. The tariff takes effect July 22, 2026, impacting agribusiness and manufacturing, while the Brazilian government rejected the U.S. justification and pledged to challenge it at the WTO and invoke the Reciprocity Law.

item.title: Zema ironiza palanque do PT em MG: 'Patrus aceitou para ter sossego'
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais, mocked the PT's difficulty in building a political platform in the state, suggesting that deputy Patrus Ananias (PT) agreed to run for governor merely to 'have a little peace'.

item.title: Zema chama candidato do PT ao governo de MG de “fantoche”
item.description: Former governor Romeu Zema (Novo) criticized the PT for selecting federal deputy Patrus Ananias as its candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, calling him a 'puppet' and claiming the left is 'practically forgotten' in the state. He said the PT struggled to form a competitive ticket, having been rejected by Rodrigo Pacheco (PSD) and Marília Campos (PT) before settling on Ananias. Zema projected that the 2026 state gubernatorial race will be contested between right-wing and center-right candidates, citing a potential joint PL-Republicanos ticket.

item.title: "O Brasil não aguenta mais quatro anos de cotas", afirma Zema em SP
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate for president from the Novo party, criticized racial quota policies, promised to privatize Petrobras, and attacked the Supreme Court, specifically Justices Alexandre de Moraes and Gilmar Mendes, during a national party meeting in São Paulo. He advocated ending 'privileges' involving politicians and magistrates, proposed reclaiming territories from criminal factions, and pushed for the impeachment of STF justices to attract Bolsonaro supporters. Zema also noted his poll numbers rose after debates in 2018 and said his future running mate must have a clean record.

item.title: Zema: “Vamos começar privatizando a Petrobras e o Banco do Brasil”
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and pré-candidate of the Novo party for Presidency, stated he intends to privatize Petrobras and Banco do Brasil if elected in 2026. The declaration was made during the National Meeting of the party in São Paulo, where he argued that proceeds from the sales would be used for other public purposes. The proposal reinforces Novo's liberal agenda, focused on reducing the state's role in the economy.

item.title: Novo negocia com Podemos vice para chapa presidencial de Zema
item.description: The national president of Novo, Eduardo Ribeiro, stated that the party is negotiating with Podemos to form a presidential ticket with former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema for the 2026 elections. No vice-presidential candidate has been defined yet, but both sides aim to finalize the agreement by August 5, the deadline for party conventions.

item.title: Zema reforça apoio a Ricardo Salles ao Senado e diz que São Paulo atrai oportunistas
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and Novo party's presidential pre-candidate, declared his support for Ricardo Salles's Senate bid, stating that São Paulo has become a 'land of opportunists' attracting politicians from other states seeking federal office.

item.title: Marinho critica “isolamento” de Bolsonaro após restrições de Moraes
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) criticized the restrictions imposed by Minister Alexandre de Moraes on Jair Bolsonaro, calling them 'extravagant' and 'unusual', and argued they constitute 'political silencing' and 'isolation' incompatible with the Democratic State of Law. Marinho compared Bolsonaro's situation to Lula's during his imprisonment, claiming Lula received numerous visits and disseminated political statements, while Bolsonaro faces far stricter limitations, including a ban on receiving visits for political-electoral purposes and on disseminating political manifestos, even through third parties, with visits limited to lawyers, doctors, and physiotherapists for 30 days.

item.title: Jaques Wagner tenta vender terreno de R$ 15,8 mi após operação da PF
item.description: Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) attempted to sell a R$15.8 million plot of land one day after becoming a target of a Federal Police investigation into alleged bribes from Banco Master. The transfer was blocked by a Supreme Court order, which also halted the sale of a R$10 million apartment in Salvador. The land, originally bought for R$28,000 in 2000, was sold to a company tied to Grupo City (owner of Bahia’s SAF), while the apartment was sold to Marcelo Passos de Araújo, mayor of Conceição do Coité and member of União Brasil.

item.title: Nikolas, sobre decisão de Moraes: “Como levar a sério as eleições nesse país?”
item.description: Allies of Jair Bolsonaro criticized a decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who expanded restrictions on the former president, banning political-electoral visits and maintaining a 30-day suspension of family access. Nikolas Ferreira's statement questions the credibility of elections in the country amid these measures.

item.title: 18% atribuem avanço das bets ao governo Lula, diz pesquisa
item.description: A More in Common/Ipsos-Ipec poll shows 18% of respondents blame Lula's government for the growth of online sports betting (bets), while 4% blame Bolsonaro. Among Lula voters, 14% hold his government responsible, compared to 8% blaming Bolsonaro. Supporting restrictions on bets would increase voting likelihood for 24% of respondents.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que anistiados pelo 8/1 subirão rampa do Planalto
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro stated that, if elected, he will ascend the ramp of the Palácio do Planalto alongside those 'amnestied' for the January 8 acts, criticizing Minister Alexandre de Moraes for banning visits to his father and for his role in the invasion cases. He also said Bolsonaro will climb the ramp in 2027, referencing the Dosimetria Law, passed by Congress, vetoed by Lula in 2026, overridden by the Legislature, and suspended by Moraes pending STF review on constitutionality.

item.title: Zema pode deixar definição de vice para depois da convenção
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's pre-candidate for president, said the choice of his running mate may be made only after the party conventions end, by August 5. He stressed that the only requirement for the vice-presidential candidate is a clean record and mentioned talks with several parties, including Podemos, without ruling out a possible ticket with Michelle Bolsonaro (PL).

item.title: Caiado diz que, se eleito, vai propor classificar facções criminosas como organizações terroristas
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, a pre-candidate for president, stated that if elected, he would propose classifying criminal factions as terrorist organizations in Brazil. He also discussed economic plans, promising to lower interest rates to encourage investment and criticized U.S., Chinese, and EU tariffs as signs of poor governance. Caiado denied being responsible for tensions with Flávio Bolsonaro, asserting that the issues were created by Bolsonaro himself.

item.title: Flávio promete anistiar envolvidos no 8/1 e ataca Moraes: 'Tirano'
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, promised to pardon those involved in the January 8, 2023, coup attempts if elected. Speaking at a PL event in Espírito Santo, he also attacked Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, calling him a 'tyrant'.

item.title: Regra do TSE causa apagão de informações governamentais
item.description: The TSE's 'defeso eleitoral' rule, enforced three months before the 2026 elections, prompted federal and state governments to delete tens of thousands of public online contents—including health, vaccination, and social benefit information—due to fears of being interpreted as premature campaigning. Even communications over 20 years old were removed, hindering citizen access to essential services. EBC also restricted over 100,000 publications and is seeking reversal from the TSE.

item.title: Clarita Maia na Crusoé: O manifesto da Casa Apostólica e da Frente Evangélica
item.description: Evangelical leaders from the Apostolic House and the Evangelical Parliamentary Front released on July 8, 2026 a manifesto addressed to the Jewish community and Brazilian society, aiming to strengthen interfaith dialogue and highlight ethical and social commitments. Though not formally political, the text carries symbolic weight in the 2026 election context, particularly due to evangelical-Jewish articulations amid rising social tensions.

item.title: Brasil apodrece às vésperas da eleição
item.description: The text argues that Brazil is facing a deep crisis of credibility and ethics, with roots tracing back to Dilma Rousseff's election and the mensalão scheme, worsened by the perception that Operation Car Wash, despite its potential for purification, failed to reverse institutional decay. The author suggests the country is 'rotting' on the eve of the 2026 elections, reflecting accumulated wear on the political class and public trust. The critique centers on the persistence of corruption and the failure of institutions to deliver genuine democratic renewal.

item.title: Por coerência, Moraes deveria impedir Michelle de falar com Bolsonaro
item.description: The article criticizes Justice Alexandre de Moraes for banning Jair Bolsonaro's sons from visiting him for 30 days, arguing that if the goal is to prevent Bolsonaro from interfering in elections, Michelle Bolsonaro should also be barred from contacting him. It notes that Michelle recorded a 27-minute video mentioning Bolsonaro repeatedly, launched a political movement, and influenced alliances—such as Celina Leão’s Senate candidacy—suggesting Bolsonaro was aware and involved. The measure’s coherence is questioned, as Michelle acts as a direct channel of influence.

item.title: Em evento, Bia Kicis e Celina Leão defendem candidatura de Michelle
item.description: At the launch event for Celina Leão's pre-candidacy for Governor of the Federal District, federal deputy Bia Kicis and Celina herself defended Michelle Bolsonaro's pre-candidacy for the Federal Senate. Celina said she is 'talking' with Michelle but stressed no final decision has been made, while Bia Kicis declared Michelle is a Senate pre-candidate and that she and Celina are 'closed' on the ticket. Bia also endorsed Flávio Bolsonaro for President, linking Celina's election to the DF governorship with Flávio's election to the presidency.

item.title: Suspenso pelo Republicanos, Manga mantém apoio à esposa, filiada ao União Brasil
item.description: Sorocaba Mayor Rodrigo Manga was suspended from the Republicans party for supporting his wife Sirlange Maganhato's candidacy for federal deputy, who is affiliated with União Brasil. Despite the suspension, Manga stated he does not intend to leave the party and reaffirmed his support for his wife's campaign.

item.title: Juíza nega pedido de Flávio Bolsonaro para indenização de R$ 61 mil
item.description: Judge Gabriela Jardon of Brasília's 6th Civil Court denied Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's R$ 61,000 defamation claim against a social media profile that labeled him a 'criminal', 'money launderer', 'militiaman', and 'thief'. The judge ruled the defendant merely expressed opinions based on prior news reports without fabricating false facts, and emphasized that as a hyperpublic figure and presidential pre-candidate, Bolsonaro must tolerate stronger political criticism. His defense announced plans to appeal.

item.title: PT intensifica bombardeio a Flávio Bolsonaro nas redes sociais
item.description: The PT has intensified social media attacks against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL’s pre-candidate for president and Lula’s main rival, accusing him of treason, conspiring in the U.S. to undermine Brazil’s PIX system, and appearing alongside a figure linked to financial fraud. The campaign is led by Pedro Rousseff, Dilma Rousseff’s nephew, aiming to exploit Bolsonaro’s weakening pre-campaign, as polls show him trailing Lula 37% to 45%. PT militants are urged to share the content to amplify the damage to Bolsonaro’s image.

item.title: Salles chama Marina de “tartaruga do Acre” e Lula de “filho da puta”
item.description: Ricardo Salles, pre-candidate for the Senate in São Paulo from the Novo party, used offensive language by calling President Lula a 'son of a bitch' and Marina Silva a 'turtle escaped from Acre' during a party event. He also attacked Simone Tebet, André do Prado, and the Centrão, positioning himself as a right-wing alternative amid Bolsonaro family support for Prado.

item.title: A estratégia de quase ministro de Lula para ampliar chances em corrida ao Senado
item.description: Deputy Pedro Lucas, leader of União Brasil in the Chamber, is seeking to align himself with Lula to boost his Senate campaign in Maranhão, despite not accepting a ministerial post due to party leadership opposition. Although União Brasil has opposed the government, Lucas is requesting archival photos with the president for campaign use, capitalizing on Lula’s 60% voter intention in the state per Real Time Big Data. This contrasts with Flávio Bolsonaro’s 22% support in the same poll.

item.title: Comissão aprova reembolso de passagem em caso de doença ou morte
item.description: The Transportation and Communications Committee of the Chamber of Deputies approved a bill granting passengers the right to cancel airline tickets with full refund or credit for rescheduling, without fines, in cases of serious illness, accident, or death of close relatives, provided the airline is notified up to 12 hours before departure. The bill establishes objective criteria for proof, such as death certificates or medical reports, and removes airlines’ discretion in accepting documentation. The proposal must still be reviewed by the Consumer Defense and Constitution and Justice committees before advancing to a full vote in Chamber and Senate.

item.title: Moro defende redução da maioridade penal após ataque a tiros no Paraná
item.description: Sergio Moro (PL-PR), pre-candidate for governor of Paraná, advocated for reducing the age of criminal responsibility following a shooting in Campo Mourão that left three dead, suggesting a possible adolescent perpetrator. He labeled the incident a 'homicidal attack' and demanded severe punishment, aligning with Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL) public security agenda. Moro leads Paraná vote intention polls with 39.9%, ahead of Requião Filho (PSD).

item.title: Moraes rejeita pedido para visita de Javier Milei a Bolsonaro durante prisão domiciliar
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes denied the request by Jair Bolsonaro's defense to receive a visit from Argentine President Javier Milei during Bolsonaro's house arrest. The decision upholds restrictions imposed after Bolsonaro was found to have violated house arrest conditions, allowing only lawyer and health professional visits. Despite Milei's scheduled trip to Brazil for a Liberal Party event, the meeting will not be permitted.

item.title: Novo diz que eleição de 2026 é a mais importante desde redemocratização
item.description: Eduardo Ribeiro, national president of the Partido Novo, declared that the 2026 election is the 'most important since re-democratization' during the party's National Meeting in São Paulo. He stressed the need to prevent a prolonged PT government, calling 24 years in power unjust for future generations, and claimed Novo is the only party with principles, while others have a 'price'. Ribeiro acknowledged the party's underperformance in 2022 due to internal issues but said 2026 will feature a more organized structure with Romeu Zema as the presidential pre-candidate.

item.title: Brasil pede fim da 6x1, mas Flávio Bolsonaro oferece Jair livre
item.description: Brazil debates ending the 6x1 work schedule, while Senator Flávio Bolsonaro suggests former President Jair Bolsonaro could be cleared to run again in 2026, sparking debate over eligibility and campaign priorities.

item.title: Michelle reforça esquema de segurança após equipe identificar aumento de ataques nas redes
item.description: The security team for former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro has strengthened her protection detail after detecting a rise in online attacks that may be inciting real-world hostility. Measures include increasing personnel, revising operational protocols, and adjusting movement strategies due to concerns about a 'copycat effect' in a politically radicalized climate. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s recent interview, in which he discussed his political break with Michelle, raised alerts not because it was seen as a threat, but due to its potential to amplify hostility in an already volatile environment.

item.title: Jaques Wagner tentou vender terreno de R$ 15,8 milhões após ser alvo no Caso Master
item.description: Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) attempted to sell a R$15.8 million plot of land in Salvador's metropolitan area one day after being targeted by the Federal Police in the Master case. The transaction was blocked by a Supreme Court order from Minister André Mendonça, who declared the property unavailable. Wagner denies any wrongdoing, stating the sale was legitimate and that his focus remains on his electoral campaign.

item.title: Presidentes de partido têm salário de até R$ 52,5 mil por mês; veja valores
item.description: In 2025, Brazilian political parties paid up to R$ 52,5 thousand monthly to ten of their national presidents, totaling R$ 2.95 million, with 96% of the funds coming from the Party Fund, largely composed of public money. The highest payment went to Ovasco Roma Altimari Resende (PRD) at R$ 630.5 thousand annually, followed by José Luiz Penna (PV) at R$ 501.4 thousand. No specific law governs these payments, though experts suggest applying the constitutional ceiling for public officials as a reference.

item.title: “Meu pai está num cativeiro”, diz Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend visits to Jair Bolsonaro for 30 days. He described the measure as a 'captivity,' stating his father is not under house arrest but in captivity. The former deputy, currently in the United States, also claimed the Constitution is being disrespected.

item.title: A mais recente polêmica provocada por Janja da Silva
item.description: In November 2024, First Lady Janja da Silva caused international embarrassment by insulting Elon Musk at the G20 Social. In May 2025, she criticized TikTok's algorithm during an official ceremony with Chinese President Xi Jinping, sparking another controversy over diplomatic protocol breach. Following her interview claiming Brazil 'never had a first lady who worked effectively,' reactions highlighted the legacy of Ruth Cardoso, wife of FHC, whose work in health, education, and social inclusion was rediscovered on social media.

item.title: Após decisão de Moraes, Eduardo Bolsonaro diz que seu pai “está num cativeiro”
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro, a federal deputy stripped of office and living in self-exile in the U.S., said his father Jair Bolsonaro is 'in captivity' following a decision by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes to suspend 'political-electoral' visits to the former president until the end of the 2026 elections. The measure, which bans general visits for 30 days (except for doctors, physiotherapists, and lawyers), was prompted by Flávio Bolsonaro's dissemination of the 'Letter to Brazilians,' which the STF ruled was an attempt to circumvent communication restrictions imposed on Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a sentence for attempted coup. The PGR supported the decision, stating the letter aimed to influence the electoral public.

item.title: Moraes nega pedido de Bolsonaro para receber visita de Milei
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied Jair Bolsonaro’s request to receive a visit from Argentine President Javier Milei, citing restrictions on visits with electoral purposes. The ruling maintains Bolsonaro’s house arrest, which has allowed 185 visits since its inception, and states that the medical basis for the restriction is no longer transient. Milei had planned to visit Bolsonaro on July 25 to support the launch of Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign.

item.title: Leia a íntegra de decisão que proíbe visita de Milei a Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied Jair Bolsonaro's defense request to receive a visit from Argentine President Javier Milei on July 25, 2026, upholding a 30-day suspension of non-essential visits. The decision followed the public reading of a letter by Flávio Bolsonaro deemed to contain political and electoral content, violating penal execution rules. Milei was scheduled to attend the PL national convention and the launch of Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio avaliam que veto a encontros políticos com Bolsonaro dificulta articulação às vésperas das convenções
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro say the Supreme Court's ban on political-electoral meetings with Jair Bolsonaro hinders final campaign coordination ahead of party conventions, particularly in ten states where pending issues remain. Alexandre de Moraes' decision to restrict visits and political manifesto dissemination is seen as obstructing the ex-president's central role in defining alliances and campaign strategy for the PL.

item.title: 'Culpa pelo tarifaço' x 'defesa da soberania': tarifa dos EUA traz 'debate equilibrado' entre direta e esquerda nas redes
item.description: The 25% US tariff on Brazilian products sparked a balanced debate on social media, with 34% of posts from the right, 34% from the left, and 32% from the press, according to Instituto Democracia em Xeque. The right blamed Lula for provoking the US through ideological negotiation, while the left defended national sovereignty, criticizing Trump and accusing Bolsonaro allies. Mobilization peaked on July 16, with public exchanges between Mauro Vieira and Marco Rubio, and the term 'Tariflávio' gained traction across the political spectrum.

item.title: Decisão de Moraes é silenciamento de Bolsonaro, diz campanha de Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign coordinator, Rogério Marinho, criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend political visits to jailed ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, calling it an unprecedented attempt at political silencing. Marinho advocated for electing Flávio Bolsonaro as president and a 'strong Senate' to restore democratic normality, emphasizing Bolsonaro's prior focus on placing allies in the Senate to influence Supreme Court appointments and impeachment proceedings.

item.title: Izabela Patriota na Crusoé: O revisionismo do sufrágio feminino
item.description: Izabela Patriota critiques the revisionism surrounding women's suffrage, emphasizing that although the achievement of voting rights for women was a historic milestone, its universality and permanence in liberal democracies are now being questioned. The article notes that New Zealand was the first country to grant women's suffrage nationally in 1893, while Brazil only did so in 1932. Despite decades of consolidation, the issue has re-entered public discourse as if it were a fragile or contingent gain.

item.title: Marinho critica decisão de Moraes: “Sem precedentes na história recente do país”
item.description: Senate opposition leader Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes’ decision to suspend visits to Jair Bolsonaro for 30 days, calling it extravagant, unusual, and without precedent in the country’s recent history. The ruling was issued due to concerns over potential undue influence or obstruction of justice linked to investigations into the January 8 attacks.

item.title: Moraes rejeita pedido de visita de Milei a Bolsonaro após endurecer regras da prisão domiciliar
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes rejected the request for Argentine President Javier Milei to visit former President Jair Bolsonaro, after tightening house arrest rules and suspending all social visits for 30 days. The decision followed Bolsonaro's violation of precautionary measures by issuing a letter supporting his son Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential pre-candidacy, which was later shared on social media. Only visits from doctors, physiotherapists, and lawyers remain authorized.

item.title: Moraes nega autorização a visita de Milei em prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied former President Jair Bolsonaro permission to receive Argentine President Javier Milei and a delegation from Argentina at his residence, where he is under house arrest. The meeting was scheduled for April 25 at 4 p.m.

item.title: Moraes rejeita pedido de Bolsonaro para receber Milei
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied a request by Jair Bolsonaro's defense to allow him to meet Argentine President Javier Milei at his residence, where he is under house arrest. Moraes ruled the meeting incompatible with the precautionary measures imposed on the former president.

item.title: 'Silenciamento político', diz coordenador de pré-campanha de Flávio sobre decisão de Moraes que amplia restrições contra Bolsonaro
item.description: Rogério Marinho, coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign, criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to tighten restrictions on former president Jair Bolsonaro, banning visits with political-electoral purpose until the end of the 2026 elections and prohibiting the dissemination of political manifestos. Marinho labeled the measures 'extravagant' and 'unprecedented,' claiming they constitute 'political silencing' that undermines the Democratic Rule of Law and exceeds constitutional limits. The ruling followed Flávio Bolsonaro's dissemination of a letter from his father endorsing his presidential bid, which violated prior precautionary measures.

item.title: Entenda o que é a Lei da Reciprocidade e como ela pode ser aplicada contra os EUA
item.description: The United States imposed a 25% tariff on Brazilian products, particularly affecting agribusiness and reviving debate over Brazil’s Economic Reciprocity Law, enacted in April 2025. The law allows Brazil to impose trade countermeasures against countries applying unilateral barriers that harm national competitiveness. President Lula stated the government will respond to U.S. actions, emphasizing national sovereignty and refraining from specifying measures until the U.S. government clarifies its position.
